title: Part XII
author: David Hume
summary: Left alone with Cleanthes, Philo admits that the design of nature strikes every mind, and argues that the quarrel between theist and atheist is largely verbal. He condemns vulgar superstition and its harms to morality and society, and ends by recommending philosophical scepticism as the first step to being a believing Christian. Pamphilus judges that Cleanthes comes nearest the truth.
